lines.line: In January 2025, the head of the most famous AI company in the world posted something strange.
"Insane thing," Sam Altman wrote. "We are currently losing money on OpenAI Pro subscriptions."
The plan cost two hundred dollars a month. And some people used so much that they cost OpenAI more than they paid.
The strangest part? He'd picked the price himself.
But this isn't a story about one plan, or one company.
Behind almost every AI subscription you pay for, there's a quiet bet. A bet that you won't use too much.
Then AI agents arrived. And "too much" stopped meaning what it used to.
This October, the small print changed again.
